hook.text: The leading plan for permanent disposal is deep geological repositories—burying waste hundreds of meters in stable rock.

buildup.text: Finland's Onkalo facility is the world's first—tunneled 430 meters into 1.8-billion-year-old granite bedrock.

discovery.text: Waste is sealed in copper canisters, surrounded by bentonite clay, then entombed in rock—barriers for millennia.

twist.text: The challenge isn't engineering—it's politics. Nobody wants a nuclear waste repository near their community.

climax.text: The US planned Yucca Mountain for decades—but political opposition killed the project despite billions spent.

quiz.question: Where is the world's first deep geological repository being built?
